title: The Father and His Two Daughters
text:
A man had two daughters. One had married a gardener, the other a man who made tiles and bricks. Some time after the weddings, the father set out to see how they were getting on.

He went first to the gardener's house. His daughter told him that everything was going well and that she had only one wish: a good heavy rain, so that the plants would be well watered and the crops would thrive.

A little later he visited the daughter married to the tile maker. She, too, said she wanted for nothing. Her one wish was for the dry weather to last, with a hot bright sun, so that the bricks and tiles laid out in the yard would bake hard.

The father went home thinking about the two answers. If one daughter wanted rain and the other wanted sunshine, he said to himself, which of them was he supposed to join in praying for?
lesson: Children who build different lives will want different things. A parent cannot take every side at once, and sometimes the best course is to love both without choosing.
people: A father, a gardener's wife, a potter's wife
